I love this game. Sure, it’s probably meant for kids (It’s really dark in some areas) but it’s all around good. At first, I didn’t understand why a lot of my friends gave it so much praise but then as I began to learn the controls better, I suddenly understood why.

Let’s see… complaints…

Honestly, I can only think of one complaint for once, that being that it feels slightly unpolished, but I’ll get into that soon. The game oozes with Charm and dev commitment. Everything seems like it’s in its rightful place and the world seems… just good gosh damn. I spent a good amount of time jumping around Mafia island because I loved its landscape so much.
As for the unpolished stuff: every so often I noticed something which made me go “eeeh, please fix?”. Two instances come to mind; the camera and a bit of the animation.

The camera is easy as heck to control, but what I don’t understand is why you can’t make it go up or down without pressing the Y button. That just seemed cheap to me. Also, the animation; some of it seems a bit stiff but it’s hardly noticeable. Although, I do remember commenting on how the Hat Kid’s hands looked disconnected from her arms while she was walking during the opening cutscene. But seriously, all that is pretty minor stuff. Any thing it gets wrong is minor at it’s worst. It’s just a dang good game.

Key Highlights:

Re-mastered for high resolution displays 1080p+ 
Enhanced visual engine with improved terrain textures, water, fire and ambient lighting effects

****************************************************************************************************
Age of Empires II HD Edition is nothing but a money grab, targeting people like me and you who enjoyed this game as kids, saying the game has "improved" and charging $20 for it.

Because for many different reasons I'm disappointed with AoE II HD and I dont recommend if you're looking into a really improved AoE II especially if youre into historical/cultural accuracy, except for some graphical upgrades!

I remember playing AoE & AoE II as a kid, and still have the original Discs with original covers, theyre great games and fun, but I wouldnt say the same thing for AoE II HD Edition, because I dont really see improvements to justify the $20 bucks.

First of all, there are many different nations to play but many of them STILL share the same 3D models! Same buildings, structures, units even though they are different nations and had different architecture and style.

Developers didn't bother to create new 3D-models and improve the game (As they wrote in key features), instead they slightly upgraded the engine and the graphics.

I've asked them about these issues, they responded and told it's not going to be easy to create new 3D-models as it requires skill, time and a lot of cash. 

But in my opinion if Modders are able to create their own models and import them into the game it should be a piece of cake for developers to do that, and if they cant do that Im sorry but they should look for a new job.

I was hoping for improvements over the original ones but sadly those flaws are still there, and its very annoying for this age, Byzantine Empire monastery is actually a mosque (This is unforgivable), then Ottomans have the ability to recruit Chivaliers (SERIOUSLY?)
These are just 2 examples, there are dozens of and many other flaws such as Multiplayer problems.

I also note that its not something really "HD" other than Widescreen support and slightly upgraded graphics.

Original Age of Empires & Age of Empires II sure are great games, I enjoy them myself but I dont recommend the HD edition unless you really want to bring some nostalgia and dont have the original discs and dont mind to throw $20 on it.

I will edit this review and write more about this game later on, thats all for now.

I wanted to like this game, I really did...

Doom was the first FPS game I ever played; I grew up on Doom 1 and 2. I loved them, and still have fond memories of them. This game just didn't have the same feelings as those ones did... Felt like every other FPS out there. I was very dissappointed.

If you like FPS games and want to try one with a similar theme, this game might be worth a try... But if you are looking for something that FEELS like the immersive world you experienced playing the original Doom (isolated, hell being unleashed, isolating backdrops with towering mountains and darkness), this is not for you.
